title: Unified orchestration agent for model rollouts (canary, A/B, shadow) and automated rollback
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Motivation: customers running Redwood in production want a single, auditable way to perform gradual model rollouts across hosted, dedicated, and private modes. Current practices spread logic across the control plane, SDKs, and ad-hoc scripts; that leads to inconsistent canaries, missing metrics for decisions, and slow emergency rollbacks. This PR introduces an orchestration agent (rollout-controller) that centralizes canary/A-B/shadow traffic policies, enforces safety checks, and wires automated rollback rules to eval and SLO signals.

What this change contains (high level):
- rollout-controller service: reconciles Rollout CRD-like objects stored in the control plane and drives traffic mutation via the routing layer. Supports canary steps, parallel A/B allocations, shadow mirroring, and scheduled rollouts.
- Policy engine: safety rules (latency regression thresholds, error-rate windows, quality regression tied to eval sets). Policies are pluggable and ship with default safe presets for low-latency, high-throughput workloads.
- Metrics & alert hooks: emits rollout-specific metrics (rollout_step_success, rollback_reason, canary_latency_delta_p50/p95, shadow_divergence_score) and creates tracing spans for each decision.
- Automated rollback: declarative rollback policies allow automatic revert on metric breaches, or escalate to manual approval if configured.
- Integration with Redwood Console: new rollout timelines and per-step graphs (docs in docs/rollouts.md).

Design summary: the controller stores a Rollout object (json schema stored in control plane) with steps. Each step can declare traffic_percentage, evaluation_queries, wait_duration, and rollback_policy. The controller reconciles desired vs actual traffic using existing routing APIs (no direct changes to router binary) so this is a control-plane-only change. To avoid noisy flaps, we implement hysteresis and rate-limited traffic changes.

Example Rollout JSON (illustrative, single-line in description): {"name":"model-embed-v2-rollout","target_model":"embed-v2","steps":[{"traffic":5,"wait":"15m","eval":"smoke-embed-set","rollback_on":["latency>+30%","quality<-2%"]},{"traffic":25,"wait":"30m"},{"traffic":100}]}

Implementation notes: initial reconciliation loop lives in cmd/rollout-controller/main.go, core logic in internal/rollout/controller.go, policy predicates in internal/rollout/policies.go, and metric/trace plumbing under internal/observability/rollout. No changes to model-serving runtime binaries were required; we reuse the routing API (control-plane call to /routing/v1/modify).

Testing and CI: unit tests included for policy predicates and decision paths; an end-to-end integration test simulates a canary with a synthetic latency regression to assert the controller triggers rollback. The pipeline initially failed a flaky e2e test (race on fake timers); fixed by moving to a deterministic clock abstraction. CI summary below.

Deployment plan: staged rollout of the rollout-controller itself via Dedicated Canary (replica-once) then full rollout. Default auto-rollback is enabled but opt-out via rollout.metadata. We will gate GA on 2 weeks of production telemetry with <1 incident over canaries and stable false-positive rate on rollback alerts.

Migration notes: existing ad-hoc rollout scripts will continue to work for 90 days; we will provide an import tool to convert them to Rollout objects recorded in the control plane.

Security/perm model: controller requires a new granular policy scope: routing.rollouts.{read,write,audit}. RBAC rules added to rbac-policy-bundle.

Related Linear/PM items: ENG-8421, ENG-8557 (rollback telemetry), PM-341.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] unit tests, [x] e2e test (flaky fixed), [x] docs updated (docs/rollouts.md), [x] console widgets wired (feature flag behind rollout-ui-alpha), [x] release notes

Notes on choices: chose control-plane-only approach to avoid per-runtime upgrade; this allows immediate safety patches and easier auditing. Hysteresis threshold is conservative by default to avoid oscillation.

Risk and mitigations: 1) Risk: controller mis-evaluates quality metrics due to noisy eval sets. Mitigation: rollouts can require multiple independent eval queries and configurable quorum. 2) Risk: runaway rollbacks during infra blips. Mitigation: the policy engine has debounce windows and requires sustained violations for automatic rollback.

CI timeline (single-line summary): first CI run failed on e2e flakiness; subsequent commits fixed deterministic clock and retriggered; final CI: all checks passed (unit, lint, e2e, integration).

Users impacted: platform engineers, release engineers, and SREs; no direct breaking API changes for customers.

Long description ends.

f7a8b9c: add e2e test and fix flaky timer by using deterministic clock abstraction
c0ffee1: docs: add docs/rollouts.md and console wiring notes
release_notes: Adds rollout-controller: declarative canary/A-B/shadow rollouts with automated rollback policies and Observatory metrics; safe defaults for production; migration tool for ad-hoc rollouts; console timeline UI behind feature flag.
review_comments: Nina Patel: Left a few nits on config validation. We should fail fast if a rollout is missing eval queries for canaries that are >10% traffic.
Jordan Lee (author): addressed in commit d4e5f6a — added validation and clear error messages. Also documented in docs/rollouts.md
Carlos Mendez: Concerned about cascading rollbacks when a downstream metrics pipeline lags. Suggest adding a lag-tolerance field.
Jordan Lee: Added lag_tolerance setting with default 2m and unit tests to assert behavior (commit f7a8b9c).
Eve Sun: Approved after verifying e2e that automatic rollback triggers on sustained latency regression.
